newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly up, wheat gains cited.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly up, wheat gains cited.

text.p: CBOT soy products ended mostly higher on Monday, boosted by limit gains in wheat, traders said.

Wheat futures surged the 20-cent per bushel limit on the open after temperatures fell to record lows in key hard red winter wheat growing areas over the weekend, putting developing wheat crops at risk of winterkill.

Soymeal faltered in early trade and the August contract closed lower on followthrough selling from Friday's near-limit losses. Traders pointed to technical indicators that were giving off bearish signals.
Some traders said Friday's near-limit losses completed a head-and-shoulders chart formation which is considered a bearish signal.

Weather was also considered bearish. Forecasts called for continued cool weather in much of the U.S. Midwest, leading to speculation that corn plantings will be delayed and farmers will be forced to switch intended corn acreage to soybeans. Soybeans can be planted later than corn.
Soymeal ended $0.90 per ton higher to $0.70 lower with May up $0.90 at $275.70. Soyoil ended 0.17 to 0.06 cent per lb higher with May up 0.06 at 23.90.

But some fundamental traders continued to look at USDA's ending stocks outlook for a tight 125 million bushel soybean carry-out. They also cited reports of drought damage to Brazilian and Argentine soybeans.

Safras e Mercado on Monday cut its estimate for Brazil's soybean output to 26.22 million tonnes from 26.88 million. A 700,000 tonne drop in Rio Grande do Sul accounted for most of the decline, Safras said.

On the day, commercials were mostly on the buy side of soymeal and soyoil while funds were on both sides. Cargill Inc bought 500 lots May soyoil and 100 July, Smith Barney bought 400 July and Merrill Lynch and Lehman Brothers each bought 300 July, put sources said.

In soymeal, Dean Witter sold 500 lots May, Rosenthal Collins sold 300 July and Refco Inc and Prudential Securities each sold 200 July. Continental Grain bought 100 May and 200 July while Cargill Inc bought 100 May and sold 200 May.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Friday's actual volume of 34,630 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,000 lots, against Friday's 24,511.
